item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is preferable because it provides idiomatic API documentation and a substantially stronger retry test that verifies multipart content survives replay. However, neither patch fully satisfies the frozen contract: both duplicate FilesService.Add instead of routing Upload through it, and both omit required validation and source-reader-error tests.","reasons":["B documents the exported Upload method; A leaves an exported API without a Go doc comment.","B's retry test parses and checks the multipart file contents on every attempt, directly verifying replayability. A only counts requests, so it could miss retries with an empty or corrupted body.","B separately validates empty filenames and nil content with clearer errors, while A combines both cases into one ambiguous error.","B adds useful user-facing documentation and a changelog entry for the new public API and retry behavior."],"risks_a":["Upload reimplements Add's option handling, request construction, response decoding, and missing-data error instead of calling s.Add, directly violating the required repository pattern.","No tests cover empty filenames, nil content, or source-reader failures.","The retry test never inspects the body, so it does not establish that streamed content is resent correctly after a 429."],"risks_b":["Upload still duplicates Add rather than calling s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), violating an explicit merge-contract requirement and creating future drift risk.","No tests cover validation failures or propagation of source-reader errors, despite those being explicitly required.","The retry test does not visibly set RetryAllMethods: true, so it does not precisely reproduce the reported POST-retry configuration; the recorded gates nevertheless indicate it passes in this repository's setup."]}
